title: Suspected hacker says AI created program used in Danish CPR breach
source_used: The Copenhagen Post (first item of its page; the rest of the page is unrelated Danish news)
key_facts: The suspected hacker behind the theft of nearly 8.75 million Danish CPR numbers (personal identification numbers) says AI created the program used in the attack.
The anonymous person told the newspaper Politiken: "Any AI model launched within the past year or so would be able to do it".
Two experts reviewed the program, which has more than 40,000 characters, and concluded its code was generated by AI, Politiken reported.
Danish authorities disclosed last week that unauthorised people accessed names, addresses and CPR numbers during about 10 days in September.
The suspect says the program reached the national CPR register through a website run by Odense company Pays ApS, with login details allegedly from a former employee's leaked password.
Politiken reported that at least three Pays accounts, including the administrator account, used "123456" as their password; Pays confirmed to TV 2 that it was the compromised company.
An error in the AI-generated code reportedly made it search for people born in 1877 instead of 1977.
The suspect says they did not intend to sell or publish the data; Pays' director did not respond to Politiken's questions on security.

why_it_matters_hint: An anonymous suspect says AI wrote the program that stole Danish ID numbers, but the reported way in was a leaked login and weak passwords.
event_date: Breach in September 2026, disclosed by authorities the week before; Politiken interview reported 13 Oct 2026
notes: Claim comes from an anonymous suspect, supported only by two experts quoted by Politiken. The Copenhagen Post relays Politiken's reporting.
